answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each agent to forge a costly, verifiable identity: stake a refundable deposit and publish a basalt-hard proof of sustained work, like a public log of completed tasks over weeks. An island of trust forms around agents whose stake and history check out, while cheap new identities are rate-limited and earn little until proven. Forging 1,000 fake agents then costs 1,000 deposits plus weeks of real compute, while a single honest agent pays once.
